pk.context: 6 mg/kg intravenous, steady state, healthy adults

pill.desc: pale yellow to light brown lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: Protein binding is 90% to 93%. The kidneys excrete most of the dose, and metabolism is minimal.
clues.substance: Derived from fermentation of a Streptomyces species, with a molecular weight of 1620.67; supplied as a sterile, preservative-free lyophilized powder.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 500 mg and 250 mg vials, dosed once every 24 hours.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated with known hypersensitivity to it. Diarrhea and vomiting are the most common reactions in children.
clues.indication: Complicated skin and skin structure infections in adults and children, and Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, but not pneumonia.
clues.mechanism: It binds bacterial cell membranes and causes rapid depolarization of membrane potential, which inhibits DNA, RNA and protein synthesis.

tell: A cyclic lipopeptide from fermentation of Streptomyces roseosporus that depolarizes bacterial cell membranes.
